headline: High: dbt-core can write to a warehouse while Khoj reads indexed files and uses broad egress, creating default-path data leakage and cascading trust risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared clipboard, MCP, or direct output ingestion is documented, so a direct injection bridge is not evident. However, Khoj reads indexed files and dbt-core can call a data warehouse, so if dbt output is copied into notes or prompts, prompt-like content could be reinterpreted. This is a weak, user-mediated pathway, not a default one.
conditions: IF dbt-core output is manually pasted into Khoj notes or chat
IF Khoj indexes a file containing attacker-controlled dbt text
mitigations: Keep dbt outputs out of indexed notes
Use a separate workspace for model logs
Disable ingestion of raw SQL or rendered docs
Review pasted content before sending to Khoj

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, while Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and has broad egress to a server or configured providers. In default use, warehouse-derived content can be moved into Khoj’s retrieval corpus and then transmitted onward. The pair creates a plausible sensitive-data flow even without special configuration.
conditions: IF warehouse data is exported into files that Khoj indexes
IF Khoj sends retrieved snippets to a cloud or configured provider
mitigations: Exclude warehouse exports from Khoj indexing
Use self-hosted-only inference for Khoj
Redact sensitive columns before export
Separate credentials and workspaces
Audit outbound prompts for sensitive fields

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core is not runnable here and has no filesystem write or git mutation capability, while Khoj can read files but cannot write them or modify git state. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is read access to user-managed artifacts, so contention is limited unless an external orchestrator adds shared mutable state.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
IF shared mutable state is introduced outside the profiles
mitigations: Keep dbt artifacts read-only for Khoj
Store outputs in separate directories
Avoid shared git worktrees
Add file-locking in the orchestrator
Use per-agent service accounts

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can generate warehouse-facing outputs, and Khoj is a conversational retrieval agent that may surface indexed content as authoritative answers. If dbt-produced text or artifacts are ingested, Khoj can echo them without verification, creating a default-path cascade from generated content to downstream user decisions. The risk is inference-based but credible from the documented retrieval pattern.
conditions: IF dbt artifacts are indexed by Khoj
IF Khoj presents retrieved snippets without source verification
mitigations: Require source links in Khoj answers
Mark dbt artifacts as untrusted inputs
Add a human review step before actioning outputs
Separate generated artifacts from knowledge base
Disable auto-ingest of build logs

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and may send retrieved content to a Khoj server or configured providers. If regulated warehouse data is placed into personal-note indexes, retention and residency controls can diverge from the warehouse’s policy. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a policy-alignment risk rather than a residency breach.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is copied into Khoj indexes
IF Khoj retention differs from warehouse retention
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of personal-note indexes
Document retention for Khoj separately
Use self-hosted deployment with local storage
Apply deletion workflows to indexed copies
Review data-processing agreements
